algorithm: Filter tropes by subgenre, then pick one per role (hero, conflict, world, theme). Each pick is weighted random with weight = w. Every w is 1, so all tropes are equally likely; raise a trope's w to make it come up more.

tropes.d: Never wanted command; the chain of command broke and it landed on them.
Came up from the ranks; the academy officers never let them forget it.
The only one who walked out, carrying what the others died to learn.
Solves the problem with math, spare parts, and no sleep.
Green, gifted, and thrown into the fight before training is done.
Took the blame for a disaster they didn't cause, and gets one chance to set it right.
Bends every law except the few they made for themselves.
The only one who can talk to them, and so the one everyone blames when talk fails.
Knows who owes whom in every district, and owes a few people too.
Swore off the work after it hurt someone, then the one job they can't refuse arrives.
An artificial mind learning what it owes the people who made it.
Fought a war that, from where they stand now, hasn't happened yet.
An ordinary person who stepped through the wrong door at the wrong moment.
Leads by organizing neighbors, not by giving orders.
Walks from settlement to settlement, trading skill for supper.
Saw it coming, said so, and was laughed out of the room.
Stays with the wounded when everyone else falls back.
Answerable for every life that came down the ladder after them.
The crew splits, and both sides believe they are saving the ship.
Hold the line long enough for the others to get clear.
Someone is trapped where no one is supposed to go back for them.
A misunderstanding with strangers is spiraling toward a war nobody wants.
The company knows, and it will bury anyone who proves it.
Two peoples each have a just claim to the same world.
A system built to protect has decided its makers are the threat.
Air, water, or power is failing, and the numbers don't add up for everyone.
Orbital mechanics sets the deadline, and physics doesn't negotiate.
The past keeps changing, and the hero is the only one who notices.
A crew of specialists, one impossible vault, and a reason that isn't greed.
There is not enough water, and both sides have children to feed.
Something got aboard, and no one may leave until it's found.
The orders are coming from someone who has already sold them out.
The settlement is finally thriving, which makes it worth taking.
The test runs at dawn, and only the hero understands what it will break.
Keep the envoys alive and the talks going while someone tries to sink both.
Get in, get the proof, get out without becoming what you're fighting.
Someone the hero loves died in the past; saving them could unmake everything since.
A voyage longer than a lifetime; most aboard have never seen a sky.
Something vast and old, built by no one we know of.
Far from help, short on everything, rich in promise.
A spinning town where every liter and every vote is counted.
A thousand floors up and a thousand down, and the sun only reaches the top.
The old cities are reefs now; the new ones float.
Steel corridors, watch rotations, and a war on the far side of the hull.
The center collapsed; the outposts are still holding out, and still loyal.
Their sky, their rules, and visitors who don't yet know the customs.
A handful of scientists, months from resupply, watching something they can't explain.
Towers half-standing, streets gone to forest, and some of the old machines still running.
Every choice splits the world; some branches are worse than others.
The same day, again, until it's lived right.
A city grown like a garden, and everyone has a share in it.
Endless day on one face, endless night on the other; life clings to the twilight band.
Home is behind enemy lines now, and the resistance is small.
A cratered rock with one ice field that two navies both need.
A real turning point in history, seen up close by someone who knows how it ends.
Some things are worth more than staying safe.
Personhood tested at its edges.
Strangers who choose to belong to each other.
We are caretakers of what we were given, not its owners.
Lies can be buried, but not forever.
Every act ripples, and some ripples can't be called back.
The world ended; people kept going anyway.
What we give up to be kept safe, and who decides.
The strength to spare someone who wouldn't spare you.
The universe is larger than our assumptions about it.
A promise kept when breaking it would be easy and unseen.
A past wrong, owned and paid for.
Every advance has a price, and someone pays it.
